findingsBeforeBuild.finding: Live query (parcel_record_ro, today): parcel_record's own row count is LESS than cad_property's true distinct-prop_id population for 5 of 6 CTX counties -- 48021 62,256/77,799 (80.0%), 48055 24,988/48,649 (51.4%), 48209 116,420/173,050 (67.3%), 48309 114,254/114,255 (~100%), 48453 380,917/500,307 (76.1%), 48491 282,570/602,050 (46.9%). This explains why the dispatch's own cited baseline ('Bastrop 9,556 of 77,799', 'Travis 233,236 of 500,307') uses the cad_property denominator rather than parcel_record's own count: a coverage percentage computed only against parcel_record's own row count would silently exclude every never-instantiated parcel from its own denominator, hiding an even larger gap than any single rail's unaccounted count shows. This is a free finding (DEV_PROCESS 1.4, 'two numbers that should agree and do not') that changes the instrument's design: the denominator must be the true cad_property population, and an explicit not-in-ledger-at-all count must be reported as its own category, separate from unaccounted (rail not yet processed) -- a three-state split, not two.

findingsBeforeBuild.item: 2 (buildingFootprint), root cause confirmed with a precise mechanism
findingsBeforeBuild.finding: src/jobs/parcel-record-fill.mjs (the only job that writes parcel_record_cell for CAD/jurisdiction rails) calls ingestCadOntoRecords and ingestJurisdictionOntoRecords only -- grep across src/jobs/ confirms ingestAtomsOntoRecords / applyAtomPresenceToRecord (src/lib/parcel-record-engine/ingest-existing.js, vendored from hauska-engine, ENGINE_PIN.json-governed) has ZERO callers in any job file; only its own test and the index.js barrel export reference it. The engine-side mapping is already correct (ENTITY_TYPE_TO_RAIL['building-footprint'] = 'buildingFootprint'). This is a wired mechanism with no caller -- the same doctrinal shape as PE's live-envelope-augment.ts and F-11's held writer: it reports as built because the code exists, but nothing ever runs it. Live-confirmed today: parcel_record_cell.buildingFootprint is 100% unaccounted for all six CTX counties, exact row-for-row match against each county's parcel_record total (query via split_part(place_key,':',1), avoiding a slow join).

hauska_mcp.atoms (ATOMS_DATABASE_URL) has an entity_id shape of `<county>:<propId>:footprint:<slot>` (slot is 'none' for an absence atom, otherwise a real footprint id) and a SEPARATE body.parcelNodeId field of `<county>:<propId>` -- exactly parcel_record's own placeKeyFromParts format, confirmed live for all six CTX counties (zero decimal-padded propIds found; a decimal-padded parcelNodeId form DOES exist in the atoms table for other counties, e.g. 48001, so this is not assumed globally, only confirmed for the six in scope). ingest-existing.js's indexAtomsByPlaceKey keys its map by row.entity_id verbatim -- if a caller passed the RAW atoms.entity_id through unchanged, the suffix would make every lookup miss regardless of propId grammar. The correct usage (matching the function's own generic 'entity_id' field name, which is caller-supplied, not literally the atoms table's own entity_id column) is for the job's SQL to alias body->>'parcelNodeId' AS entity_id when building the rows passed to indexAtomsByPlaceKey. This resolves the integration lane's 2026-09-06 open question (_inbox/2026-09-06_integration_building-footprint_ctx-gap_resolved.md) between 'reconciliation step never built' and 'key-grammar mismatch' -- both are true and compound: the step was never built, AND a naive implementation using the raw entity_id column would have failed silently even once built. Verified live for Bastrop specifically: 71,501 raw atom rows over 62,256 real+absence distinct parcelNodeIds, i.e. multiple real-footprint atoms per parcel are normal (a parcel can have >1 building), matching companionRows' rowCount design intent.

findingsBeforeBuild.item: 2 (buildingFootprint), real vs absence atom counts corrected, and the vendored function's own limit
findingsBeforeBuild.finding: Live counts today (real / absence / distinct-parcels-real / n=distinct-parcels-absence): 48021 24,861/46,640/15,616/46,640; 48055 24,656/10,613/14,375/10,613; 48209 41,422/87,147/29,353/87,147; 48309 54,858/71,115/43,150/71,115; 48453 72,919/323,543/57,374/323,543; 48491 163,355/145,534/137,160/145,534. These match the dispatch's real-atom figures for the five 2026-09-07 counties exactly, but the dispatch's Caldwell figure ('35,269 real atoms') is the sum of real+absence (24,656+10,613=35,269), not the real count alone -- a real atom's own body carries a nested absence object ({status, absence:{kind,reason}, ...}), and my first query used the wrong predicate (body ? 'absenceReason', which does not exist) and returned zero absence rows for every county; corrected to body ? 'absence'. distinct-real-parcels + absence-n reconciles almost exactly against each county's parcel_record total (exact match for 48021/48055/48453; within 0.1% for 48209/48309/48491), meaning the atom estate already has near-total real-or-absence coverage matching the ledger's own population -- a clean, well-evidenced foundation to build on. Separately: applyAtomPresenceToRecord/companionRows can only ever emit kind:'value' for a companion rail -- there is no branch that emits absent-verified. This is a genuine limit of the vendored engine function (cannot hand-edit; ENGINE_PIN.json), not a bug to fix here. The absence half of this job will be job-level code, following the SAME layering precedent parcel-record-fill.mjs already uses for cityLimits (ingestJurisdictionOntoRecords is job-level, not vendored, and stamps absent-verified directly) -- 'the job decides what data feeds it,' per that function's own comment.

design.coverageInstrument: New file src/lib/county-rail-coverage.mjs (pure functions, not under parcel-record-engine/ -- never touches vendored code). summarizeCountyRailCoverage({ countyFips, railKey, cadPopulation, cellCounts }) takes cellCounts = { value, 'absent-verified', 'not-applicable', refused, unaccounted } (from countCellState, already exported by the engine) plus the true cad_property population for that county, and an inLedger count (sum of cellCounts) it derives itself (measure the class, never subtract). Returns { countyFips, railKey, cadPopulation, inLedger, notInLedger: cadPopulation-inLedger, measured: value+absentVerified+refused (EARNED_CELL_KINDS, reused from cell-state.js, not re-derived), notApplicable, unaccounted, sampleSize: measured, status: sampleSize>0 ? 'measured' : 'unmeasured', pct: sampleSize>0 ? round(measured/(measured+notApplicable) *100, 2) : null }. Refuses (throws) if cadPopulation < inLedger (an impossible state signalling a wrong denominator query, never silently clamped). New file src/jobs/county-rail-coverage-report.mjs -- read-only CLI, no writer-allowlist entry needed (writes nothing): queries cad_property distinct prop_id count per county (cortex store) and parcel_record_cell cell_state counts per (county, rail) (factory store, via split_part(place_key,...) same pattern used in this checkpoint's own verification, avoiding the slow join observed earlier), for a caller-supplied rail list (default: PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS from rail-keys.js -- comprehensive by default per doc-repo-26's relayed CTX-C caution about a monotonic guard that can't see a whole dimension, not a hand-picked subset). Prints one JSON line per (county, rail), same 'last JSON line' convention as gate-rail-cli.mjs/publish-gate-sched.mjs for machine consumption.
design.buildingFootprintReconcile: New file src/jobs/parcel-building-footprint-reconcile.mjs, same module-doc convention as parcel-record-fill.mjs (Executes/Triggers/Fails/Bypasses). New writer-allowlist.mjs entry 'parcel-building-footprint-reconcile' (kind: 'atom-reconcile', planRow: 'P-124', liveRest: false). Pages parcel_record by place_key for the target county (same LANDING_PAGE_SQL-style keyset pagination already used elsewhere), loads that page's current buildingFootprint cells. Two atom queries against ATOMS_DATABASE_URL, both filtered by jurisdiction_tenant = 'tx_<county>' (indexed) and entity_type='building-footprint': (a) real, `NOT (body ? 'absence')`, grouped by body->>'parcelNodeId' with count -- rows reshaped as { entity_id: parcelNodeId, entity_type, n } and fed through the EXISTING, UNMODIFIED indexAtomsByPlaceKey + ingestAtomsOntoRecords (vendored, correct as-is for the value case); (b) absence, `body ? 'absence'`, one row per parcel with body#>>'{absence,reason}' -- fed through a new job-level function ingestBuildingFootprintAbsenceOntoRecords(records, absenceByPlace, vintage), same layering precedent as ingestJurisdictionOntoRecords (job-level, stamps kind:'absent-verified' with the atom's own reason as basis, only on cells still unaccounted after the real-atom pass). Owned-rail guard: BUILDING_FOOTPRINT_OWNED_RAIL_KEYS=['buildingFootprint'], a scoped UPSERT (same CASE-guarded never-downgrade shape as UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL) touching only that rail. --apply gated FACTORY_CLOUD=1 (LAPTOP_WRITE_FROZEN), per-county claimAndVerify/releaseClaim against Factory's own claim store (entity_type=JOB_ID), matching parcel-record-fill.mjs exactly. --twice fingerprint-drift test for idempotency, same pattern. Re-runnable by design: only ever moves unaccounted -> value/absent-verified, so a later CTX-D acquisition improvement is picked up by simply re-running this job, no special-casing needed.

preRegisteredFalsifiers: If summarizeCountyRailCoverage ever returns a non-null pct when sampleSize (measured) is 0, the instrument has the exact defect finding 1 exists to kill.

If cadPopulation < inLedger for any live county/rail pair tested, the cad_property query is wrong (a parcel can't be in the ledger without existing in the true roll) and must be fixed before trusting any output.
If a fixture with zero atoms at all for a parcel leaves its buildingFootprint cell anything other than unaccounted, the reconcile job has a defect.
If a fixture with only an absence atom for a parcel produces kind:'value' instead of 'absent-verified', the absence branch is not wired correctly.
If re-running the reconcile job twice on identical input data produces a different cell_state the second time (drift), idempotency is broken.
If the reconcile job ever downgrades an already-earned (non-unaccounted) buildingFootprint cell, the owned-rail guard has failed.
If node --test after all changes reports any failure beyond the 1008-test clean baseline recorded above, something in this lane's change broke the suite.
